sections.title: Executive Summary + Investment Thesis
sections.body:
**Executive Summary**
ICICIBANK's fiscal 2025 performance demonstrates a notable improvement, with net interest income and non-interest income increasing by 10.8% to ₹1,077.68 billion. The bank's core operating profit rose by 12.5% to ₹653.96 billion, driven by a 14.9% growth in profit before tax to ₹626.16 billion. The consolidated profit after tax and minority interest stood at ₹510.29 billion, representing a 15.3% increase from the previous year. The bank's consistent dividend payment history continues, with the Board of Directors recommending a dividend of ₹11.00 per equity share for the year ended March 31, 2025.

**Investment Thesis**
Our investment thesis for ICICIBANK is positive, driven by the bank's robust financial performance and strong reserve position. The bank's total reserves and surplus stood at ₹2,885.82 billion as of March 31, 2025, representing a significant increase from ₹2,355.89 billion in the previous year. With a profit after tax of ₹472.27 billion and a consolidated profit after tax and minority interest of ₹510.29 billion, ICICIBANK demonstrates its ability to generate strong earnings and maintain a healthy capital position. We believe that the bank's consistent dividend payment history and strong financials make it an attractive investment opportunity, with potential for long-term growth and returns.

sections.title: Business Overview + Segment Breakdown
sections.body:
ICICI Bank's business operations are categorized into five primary segments: Retail Banking, Wholesale Banking, Treasury, Other Banking, and Unallocated. As per the RBI guidelines, Retail Banking includes exposures that satisfy specific criteria such as orientation, product, granularity, and low value of individual exposures. This segment also encompasses income from credit cards, debit cards, third-party product distribution, and associated costs. Wholesale Banking comprises advances to trusts, partnership firms, companies, and statutory bodies not included under Retail Banking. The Treasury segment encompasses the Bank's entire investment and derivative portfolio. Other Banking includes leasing operations and items not attributable to any particular business segment, while Unallocated items comprise tax paid in advance, deferred tax, and provisions reckoned at the entity level.

For the year ended March 31, 2025, the segment-wise revenue from operations was: ₹1,561,846.8 million for Retail Banking, ₹824,362.1 million for Wholesale Banking, ₹1,350,525.8 million for Treasury, and ₹43,862.9 million for Other Banking, resulting in a total revenue of ₹3,780,597.6 million. After accounting for inter-segment revenue, the total revenue stood at ₹1,917,704.8 million. The segment results for the year were: ₹216,210.4 million for Retail Banking, ₹215,646.3 million for Wholesale Banking, ₹187,607.3 million for Treasury, and ₹6,698.0 million for Other Banking, totaling ₹626,162.0 million. The Bank's total assets as of March 31, 2025, were ₹21,182,399.7 million, with segment-wise assets being ₹7,929,301.9 million for Retail Banking, ₹5,482,698.2 million for Wholesale Banking, ₹7,216,955.2 million for Treasury, and ₹505,972.1 million for Other Banking.

sections.title: Financial Performance
sections.body:
The financial performance of ICICIBANK for fiscal 2025 is characterized by notable growth in key income streams and profitability metrics. As per the financial highlights, the bank's net interest income and non-interest income increased by 10.8% to ₹1,077.68 billion in fiscal 2025, from ₹972.55 billion in the preceding year. The core operating profit rose by 12.5% to ₹653.96 billion, driven by the growth in income streams, albeit partially offset by an 8.3% increase in operating expenses to ₹423.72 billion. The profit after tax for the year ended March 31, 2025, stood at ₹472.27 billion, representing a 15.5% increase from ₹408.88 billion in fiscal 2024.

On a consolidated basis, the bank's total income increased to ₹2,945.87 billion in fiscal 2025, from ₹2,360.38 billion in the previous year. The consolidated profit after tax and minority interest for the year ended March 31, 2025, was ₹510.29 billion, marking a 15.3% increase from ₹442.56 billion in fiscal 2024. The bank's financial performance is also reflected in its appropriations, with the balance carried over to the balance sheet increasing to ₹1,023.91 billion in fiscal 2025, from ₹773.78 billion in the preceding year. The board of directors has recommended a dividend of ₹11.00 per equity share for the year ended March 31, 2025, underscoring the bank's commitment to rewarding its shareholders.

sections.title: Balance Sheet Health + Cash Flow
sections.body:
The balance sheet health of ICICIBank appears robust, with total reserves and surplus standing at ₹3,104,114,654 as of 31.03.2025, representing a significant increase from ₹2,533,338,376 as of 31.03.2024. The securities premium reserve has also witnessed a substantial growth, with a closing balance of ₹606,132,791 as of 31.03.2025, up from ₹519,436,438 as of 31.03.2024. The investment fluctuation reserve has increased to ₹34,272,809 as of 31.03.2025, from ₹31,686,709 as of 31.03.2024. The balance in the profit and loss account has also risen to ₹1,183,850,670 as of 31.03.2025, from ₹898,257,800 as of 31.03.2024.

The cash flow position of the bank is not explicitly disclosed in the provided excerpts. However, the significant increase in the balance in the profit and loss account suggests a healthy accrual of profits, which can contribute to the bank's cash flow. The additions to the revenue and other reserves, including the transfer of ₹20,190,304 during the year, also indicate a robust operational performance. Nevertheless, without explicit cash flow data, a comprehensive assessment of the bank's cash flow health cannot be made.

sections.title: Management Commentary
sections.body:
The management of ICICIBANK has provided commentary on the bank's approach to risk management, highlighting its comprehensive process to identify and monitor risks. In fiscal 2025, the bank continued to monitor traditional risks such as economic, credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks, while also acknowledging emerging new-age risks due to climate change. The bank has initiated steps to embed climate risk assessment and climate risk management into its risk management framework, including the formulation of a Climate Risk Management Framework (CRMF). This framework aims to integrate climate risk into the overall risk management framework and guides the identification and assessment of both physical and transitional risks on the lending portfolio.

The management has also emphasized the importance of responding proactively to risks and opportunities to safeguard the bank's financial stability and resilience. The bank's subsidiaries have reported profits, with ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited and ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited reporting profits after tax of ₹11.89 billion and ₹25.08 billion, respectively, in fiscal 2025. The bank's net worth and profit after tax are not explicitly stated in the provided excerpts, and therefore, cannot be commented on. Overall, the management's commentary highlights the bank's focus on risk management and its efforts to mitigate potential risks, while also emphasizing the importance of responding to emerging risks and opportunities.

sections.title: Key Risks
sections.body:
The key risks faced by ICICI Bank are multifaceted and can be broadly categorized into economic, credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks. The Bank is exposed to a volatile economic environment driven by changing global monetary policy stance, uncertain global trade environment, and geopolitical tensions. Additionally, uncertainties pertaining to elevated geopolitical risks, uncertain global trade environment, and weak global growth outlook pose challenges for the Bank's customers, thereby increasing credit risk. The Bank is also susceptible to market and liquidity risks arising from changing monetary policy stance, tighter liquidity conditions, and exchange rate movements. Furthermore, the Bank has identified emerging new-age risks due to climate change, including physical and transitional risks, which are being addressed through the formulation of a Climate Risk Management Framework.

The Bank's response to these risks includes continuous monitoring of developments in the global and Indian economy, ensuring effective risk management across business segments, maintaining healthy capital and liquidity positions, and strengthening its liability franchise. The Bank also conducts periodic reviews at the Risk and Credit Committees and has implemented a comprehensive risk management framework to mitigate these risks. However, the Bank's ability to manage these risks is subject to various factors, including statutory and regulatory changes, international economic and business conditions, and increase in non-performing loans, among others, as outlined in the safe harbour statement.

sections.title: Recent Developments
sections.body:
Recent Developments

In fiscal 2025, ICICI Bank marked 70 years of service and continued to progress on its sustainable growth journey. The Bank's profit before tax excluding treasury grew by 11.4% year-on-year to ₹607.13 billion. The domestic loan portfolio delivered broad-based loan growth of 13.9% year-on-year to ₹13,109.81 billion. Deposits also grew by 14.0% year-on-year to ₹16,103.48 billion, maintaining a stable and healthy funding profile. The Bank remains focused on maintaining a resilient balance sheet with adequate liquidity, prudent provisioning, and healthy capital adequacy. 

The Bank has also been proactive in managing risks, including economic, credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks, as well as emerging new-age risks due to climate change. The Bank has initiated steps to embed climate risk assessment and climate risk management as part of its risk management framework, and has formulated a Climate Risk Management Framework (CRMF) to guide the identification and assessment of physical and transitional risks on the lending portfolio.

sections.title: Bull vs Bear vs Base Case
sections.body:
The bull case for ICICI Bank is supported by its strong financial performance in fiscal 2025, with profit before tax excluding treasury growing by 11.4% year-on-year to ₹607.13 billion. The Bank's domestic loan portfolio also exhibited broad-based growth, increasing by 13.9% year-on-year to ₹13,109.81 billion. Additionally, the Bank's deposits grew by 14.0% year-on-year to ₹16,103.48 billion, indicating a stable and healthy funding profile. These factors suggest that the Bank is well-positioned for continued growth and profitability.

In contrast, the bear case for ICICI Bank is centered on the potential risks and challenges outlined in the Bank's risk management framework, including economic, credit, market, liquidity, and operational risks. The Bank's exposure to emerging new-age risks due to climate change also poses a threat to its financial stability and resilience. For example, the Bank has identified volatile economic environment, uncertainties pertaining to elevated geopolitical risks, and weak global growth outlook as key risks. While the Bank has implemented measures to mitigate these risks, such as continuous monitoring and periodic reviews, the bear case scenario assumes that these risks may materialize and negatively impact the Bank's performance. The base case scenario assumes that the Bank will continue to execute its business strategy effectively, balancing growth with risk management, and delivering moderate growth in profitability and loan portfolio, with profit before tax excluding treasury and domestic loan portfolio growth rates in line with historical trends.

Income and expenditure items of integral foreign operations (representative offices) are translated at daily closing rates, and income and expenditure items of non-integral foreign operations (foreign branches, offshore banking units and foreign subsidiaries) are translated at quarterly average closing rates. Monetary foreign currency assets and liabilities of domestic and integral foreign operations are translated at closing exchange rates notified by Foreign Exchange Dealers’ Association of India (FEDAI) relevant to the balance sheet date and the resulting gains/losses are recognised in the profit and loss account. Both monetary and non-monetary foreign currency assets and liabilities of non-integral foreign operations are translated at relevant closing exchange rates notified by FEDAI at the balance sheet date and the resulting gains/ losses from exchange differences are accumulated in the foreign currency translation reserve until the disposal of the net investment in the non-integral foreign operations. Pursuant to RBI guideline, the Bank does not recognise the cumulative/proportionate amount of such exchange differences as income or expenses, which relate to repatriation of accumulated retained earnings from overseas operations, in the profit and loss account. Contingent liabilities on account of guarantees, endorsements and other obligations denominated in foreign currencies are disclosed at the closing exchange rates notified by FEDAI relevant to the balance sheet date. 7. Foreign exchange and derivative contracts Derivative transactions comprises of forward contracts, futures, swaps and options. The Group undertakes derivative transactions for trading and hedging balance sheet assets and liabilities. WICICIBank

RESPONDING TO RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES The Bank has a comprehensive process to identify and monitor risks and respond appropriately. The Bank continuously reviews and enhances the methods for identification and assessment of risks, sets appropriate metrics and controls, and mitigants for managing significant risks. In fiscal 2025, the Bank continued to monitor the risks it is exposed to, including economic, credit, market, liquidity and operational risks. Apart from these traditional risks, the Bank is also cognisant of emerging new-age risks due to climate change. The Bank has initiated steps to embed climate risk assessment and climate risk management as part of the Bank’s risk management framework. The Bank has formulated a Climate Risk Management Framework (CRMF) for integration of climate risk into overall risk management framework and it guides on identifying and assessing the impact of both physical and transitional risks on the lending portfolio. The framework will undergo periodic reviews to ensure alignment with available regulatory climate risk guidance, reflecting the evolving understanding and assessment of climate risk. The Bank has also been participating in policymaking by providing inputs and supporting the regulator in assessing impact of climate change risks on specific sectors. Risk Type Key Risks Our Response Understanding and responding proactively to risk and opportunities enables the Bank to safeguard its financial stability and resilience. Economic Risk Volatile economic environment driven by changing global monetary policy stance, uncertain global trade environment driven by US tariffs and geopolitical tensions. Continuous monitoring developments in the global and Indian economy including country risk, sector-specific risks and responding accordingly. Periodic reviews at Risk and Credit Committees. Credit Risk Uncertainties pertaining to elevated geopolitical risks, uncertain global trade environment driven by US tariffs, continuing high interest rates for longer periods though with changing monetary policy stance and weak global growth outlook across the world posed challenges for customers. Ensuring effective risk management across business segments, close monitoring of the portfolios for early identification of assets under watch, strengthening by ongoing reviews and stress testing; maintaining healthy capital and liquidity positions, which are well above regulatory requirements. Market and Liquidity Risk Risks posed by changing monetary policy stance, tighter liquidity conditions for a substantial portion of the year and exchange rate movements. Comprehensive policies and periodic reviews at the level of Board and committees; strategic priority towards asset liability management and strengthening the Bank’s liability franchise. 48 | Annual Report 2024-25 f/)/CICI Bank I
